candidates.rationale: IC decays monotonically from +0.025 (2000) to +0.001 (2013) and the factor sits at rho 0.792 against its own archived sibling sharing the identical denominator. Working memory notes a window retune on this exact chassis won't decorrelate (21d/42d already rho 0.950), so the lever is which price field anchors the numerator; using $open (the actual T+1 execution price) instead of $close gives a genuinely different range-position measure.

Stability drops to 0.93 with a sign flip in 2013. Working memory flags TS_STD($high-$low,10) as a reused volatility-normalizer that only decorrelates when its own window or measure changes (numerator-only swaps already failed); lengthening the vol window from 10 to 21 smooths the late-sample instability and moves off the saturated denominator.

Working memory shows CS_RANK($book_per_share/$close) * CS_RANK(fundamental) is saturated regardless of which profitability ratio fills the second slot (roe and leverage both collided at 6 shared nodes), so the fundamental partner is not the fixable lever, the price denominator is. Swapping to the dividend-adjusted close changes the ratio's numeric history while leaving the well-behaved, perfectly-stable $roe leg untouched.

This parent sits at rho 0.798 against its own archived twin that differs only in the TS_DELTA($open,·) window (5 vs 10), right at the correlation ceiling. Since window retunes on that exact leg are already exhausted, changing the field inside TS_DELTA rather than its window is the untried decorrelating lever.

Sits at rho 0.780 against batch-mate 0168481b31dce7bc, which shares this identical TS_MEAN($return,10) reversal leg. The EPS/TS_MIN(low) engine drives the 100%-positive-years stability and should be preserved, so shortening the shared reversal window is the smallest edit that pulls the weaker, duplicated leg away from that neighbor.

Working memory closes TS_MIN($low,21)/($close+1e-8) as a fragment that collided 3 times regardless of fundamental or outer wrapper, and none of those tests varied the denominator's price field. Swapping close for open is the untested lever for this exact ratio, and also targets this parent's outlier complexity charge (0.100, far above every other candidate) without adding nodes.

Sits at rho 0.780 against batch-mate 693246746bbdc073 and shows a 2012 sign flip. Moving the EPS-yield denominator to the dividend-adjusted close diversifies away from that neighbor (which occupies the TS_MIN(low) direction) instead of converging toward it.

IC flips negative only in the final year (2013: -0.0028) after 13 straight positive years, suggesting the 21-day high-water-mark is too slow to track the late-sample regime shift. Shortening just that lookback makes the drawdown-from-high measure more adaptive while leaving the dollar-volume normalizer untouched.

Batch-worst turnover (0.294, charged 0.011) with the lowest ICIR (0.087) and a 3-day half-life is a textbook cost-not-earned-back case. Working memory already marks the TS_DELTA($open,w) leg exhausted at w=5/10 and names the vol-ratio's own windows as the untried lever, so smoothing the noisy 5-day STD leg to 10 days directly targets the turnover driver.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Check candidates against everything already proposed this run, not only the persistent archive.
